cause: Every content href field was declared z.string().url() (accepts javascript: and data:) or a bare z.string() (certification link, thesisLink, decision spec, cvUrl), so a script-scheme URL passed validate-content and rendered as a live <a href>.
context: rc-2 Job 3 review; the build-time content contract (content-schema.mjs, read by validate-content and exported as v1.json) and its dev-mode mirror (src/lib/schemas/projects.ts) declare every URL field as z.string().url(); the profile links (HeroSection) and project links render these values as <a href>
expected: every content URL field, in content-schema.mjs, its exported v1.json and the dev-mode projects schema, accepts only http: and https: URLs; javascript: and data: are rejected
repro: cd frontend && node --input-type=module -e 'import {z} from "zod"; console.log(z.string().url().safeParse("javascript:alert(1)").success)'  # prints true; content-schema.mjs uses z.string().url() for linkedinUrl, githubUrl and every project link
solution: One HttpUrl rule per schema file (url + ^https?://) on all 17 href sinks in content-schema.mjs and projects.ts; certification link also allows the # sentinel; cvUrl is a same-origin path only; v1.json regenerated with the pattern. Fix b3b14ff.
symptom: z.string().url() accepts javascript:alert(1) and data:text/html,x, and v1.json declares the same fields as format: uri, which also accepts them; ProfileSchema.safeParse({linkedinUrl:'javascript:alert(1)',...}) succeeds, so such a value passes validate-content and renders as a live link (CWE-79)
title: content URL fields accept javascript: and data: URLs

cause: 96fc100 switched the export to Zod 4 z.toJSONSchema in its default io:output mode, which emits additionalProperties:false on every object, while Zod parsing (validate path) strips unknown keys; the artifact validates input, so the two validators disagreed on the committed content.
context: rc-2 Job 3 review; validate-content.mjs:4-7 states it validates against the same schema the admin panel consumes as JSON Schema
expected: validate-content and the published v1.json agree: committed content that passes validate-content is valid against v1.json, and content the export rejects fails validate-content
repro: cd frontend && node --input-type=module -e 'import Ajv from "ajv"; import fs from "node:fs"; const v=new Ajv({allErrors:true,logger:false}).compile(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("public/content/schema/v1.json","utf8"))); console.log(v(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("public/content/en.json","utf8"))), v.errors?.[0]?.params)'  # prints false {additionalProperty:'achievements'}; ajv is the transitive copy eslint installs, not a declared dependency
solution: export-content-schema.mjs passes io:input; v1.json regenerated without the closed objects; contract test asserts no object node closes additionalProperties. Fix 9101242.
symptom: a JSON Schema validator against public/content/schema/v1.json rejects en.json, pt.json and de.json: .experiences[0].roles[0..2] should NOT have additional properties {additionalProperty: achievements}; validate-content passes because Zod strips unknown keys while the exported JSON Schema forbids them (additionalProperties: false)
title: published v1.json rejects the committed content that validate-content passes
